description:
INSTANT MONITORING
This FDA Approved with Large Screen Display Clinical Digital Wrist Blood Pressure Monitor Cuffs is designed to make your blood pressure monitoring simple, quick and easy at all times.

Why the blood pressure readings is different every time?
Human blood pressure will change in a very short time due to normal physiological reactions, so the blood pressure may also change during measuring, re-measurement should be in 5 minutes. In fact, even the same doctor continuously measures blood pressure 3-4 times, he will get a different measurement too.

Correct Blood Pressure Measurement Steps
Step 1: Relax in a quiet environment for 5 minutes before measuring blood pressure, if necessary, take a few deep breaths to keep your heart rate steady.

Step 2: Sit quietly in an upright position with legs uncrossed and feet flat on the floor.

Step 3: Keep the position of the cuff at the same height of your heart, meanwhile the cuff's tube off-center towards the inner side of the arm (in line with your pink finger) and close the cuff. The cuff shouldn't be too tight or loose. To test the cuff's fit, snugly insert one index finger between the cuff and your arm.

Step 4: Naturally put your hand on table and let your palm face up. Do not talk or move your body when measuring.

Step 5: Human blood pressure is a changing parameter. Theoretically, there will be little differences between each
measurement. It is the best, however, to re-measure once or twice and choose the average value. Re-measurement should be carried out after 5 to 10 minutes.

The blood pressure in the morning can be significantly different than at night, or when you visit a doctor’s office. Your numbers often change depending on posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions or sleep. To get a more effective and accurate assessment of your blood pressure, we suggest you to monitor your blood pressure at the same time every day with peace of mind and follow the tips before you get started.

Measurement Methods

 1. Sit comfortably in a chair with flat feet on the floor.

 2. Select your user ID (A or B).

 3. Press the Stop / Start key. The pump starts to fill the cuff. The display shows the rising cuff pressure continuously.

 4. After automatically reaching a single pressure, the pump stops and the pressure drops slowly. The cuff pressure is displayed during the measurement.

 5. When the device has detected your heart rate, the heart symbol in the display starts to flash.

 6. After completion of the measurement, the measured systolic and diastolic blood pressure values and the pulse are displayed.

While the cause of high blood pressure in most people remains unclear, a variety of conditions – such as getting little or no exercise, poor diet, obesity, older age, and genetics – can contribute to the development of hypertension.

What Is Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure?

The blood pressure reading is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is written as systolic pressure, the force of the blood against the artery walls as your heart beats, over diastolic pressure, the blood pressure between heartbeats. For example, a blood pressure reading is written as 120/80 mmHg, or “120 over 80”. The systolic pressure is 120 and the diastolic pressure is 80.

How to get accurate reading:    

The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise.Blood pressure wanders all over the map throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, meals, and moods.

We suggest to measure at around the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm 2cm (approximately 2 finger-breadths) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the centre of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull the end of the cuff so that it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ our manual as detail as possible to be instructed regularly!

Masked Hypertention & White-coat Hypertention:

Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn’t always provide accurate  information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and average them.

description:
When is the best time to measure blood pressure at home?

Blood pressure readings can fluctuate throughout the day, which makes it important to check readings several times and at different points.
Checking your BP monitor about five to six times will help you obtain a good idea of where your blood pressure lies. Establishing a routine of checking your monitor will help this effort.

One Key Operation
LCD large Screen
2 Users Total 180 Memories with Date & Time
8.6”-16.5” inch Cuff


How to Use

Place elbow on the desk
The wrist band and heart on the same level
Palm up and relax
Measure at the same time with the same arm gesture each day


Note:

Find a quiet place to check your blood pressure. You will need to listen for your heartbeat.
Make sure that you are comfortable and relaxed with a recently emptied bladder (a full bladder may affect your reading).
Roll up the sleeve on your arm or remove any tight-sleeved clothing.
Rest in a chair next to a table for 5 to 10 minutes. Your arm should rest comfortably at heart level. Sit up straight with your back against the chair, legs uncrossed. Rest your forearm on the table with the palm of your hand facing up.

Tips to Monitor Blood Pressure at Home:
The blood pressure in the morning can be significantly different than at night, or when you visit a doctor’s office. Your numbers often change depending on posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions or sleep. To get a more accurate assessment of your blood pressure, we suggest you to measure your blood pressure at the same time every day with peace of mind and follow the tips before you get started.
-Avoid food, caffeine, alcohol, or tobacco products for 30 minutes prior to measuring.
-Rest and sit up straight with your back against the chair, legs uncrossed, feet flat on the floor.
-Place your forearm on an armrest or table with palm of your hand facing up.
-After sitting quietly for five minutes, wrap the cuff snugly around the upper part of your bare left arm. The lower edge of the cuff should be about 1 inch above the bend of your elbow. Use the Velcro wrap to make the cuff snug, but not too tight.
-If you want to repeat the measurement, please wait at least 10 minutes before re-inflating the cuff.

Find the Right Cuff:
Cuff size is also very important in ensuring an accurate reading every time you monitor.
The inflatable part of the sleeve should fit around 80 percent of your upper arm.
To determine your arm size, use a cloth measuring tape and measure the circumference of your left upper arm midway between your elbow and shoulder.

The standard D-Ring cuff blood pressure monitor allows you to accurately track of your systolic/ diastolic blood pressure and heart rate with date and time stamp easily at home. The digital sphygmomanometer bp cuff fits adult arms measuring between 8.6 to 14.2 inches. Easy-to-read large LCD display allows for all ages to use, especially the seniors.

Tips to Monitor Blood Pressure at Home:
The blood pressure in the morning can be significantly different than at night, or when you visit a doctor’s office. Your numbers often change depending on posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions or sleep. To get a more accurate assessment of your blood pressure, we suggest you to measure your blood pressure at the same time every day with peace of mind and follow the tips before you get started.
-Avoid food, caffeine, alcohol, or tobacco products for 30 minutes prior to measuring.
-Rest and sit up straight with your back against the chair, legs uncrossed, feet flat on the floor.
-Place your forearm on an armrest or table with palm of your hand facing up.
-After sitting quietly for five minutes, wrap the cuff snugly around the upper part of your bare left arm. The lower edge of the cuff should be about 1 inch above the bend of your elbow. Use the Velcro wrap to make the cuff snug, but not too tight.
-If you want to repeat the measurement, please wait at least 10 minutes before re-inflating the cuff.

Find the Right Cuff:
Cuff size is also very important in ensuring an accurate reading every time you monitor.
The inflatable part of the sleeve should fit around 80 percent of your upper arm.
To determine your arm size, use a cloth measuring tape and measure the circumference of your left upper arm midway between your elbow and shoulder.

description: Product introduction:Product Name: JZ-256A Tri-color backlit arm electronic sphygmomanometer Electronic sphygmomanometer is a convenient and feasible medical device developed by using modern electronic technology and the principle of indirect blood pressure measurement. Its principle is to measure blood pressure indirectly by oscillographic method, to sense pulse wave information during deflation or inflation, and to obtain systolic and diastolic blood pressure data through a series of complex conversion and calculation. The measurement method of arm sphygmomanometer is similar to that of traditional mercury sphygmomanometer, which measures brachial artery. Because its arm band is placed on the upper arm, its measurement stability is better than wrist sphygmomanometer, and it is more suitable for older patients, arrhythmia, peripheral blood vessel aging caused by diabetes, etc. The disadvantage is that it is not as convenient as wrist electronic sphygmomanometer. Arm sphygmomanometer: It can measure arterial blood pressure correctly, and must take off its jacket for measurement. However, it is large in size and inconvenient to carry, and can use stabilized power supply. The upper arm sphygmomanometer is more accurate because the arm is close to our heart and the error is not too big, but the wrist is a little worse than the arm. Therefore, wrist electronic sphygmomanometer is not suitable for patients with blood circulation disorder. It is suggested that patients with diabetes, hyperlipidemia, hypertension and the elderly choose arm-type electronic sphygmomanometer

While the cause of high blood pressure in most people remains unclear, a variety of conditions – such as getting little or no exercise, poor diet, obesity, older age, and genetics – can contribute to the development of hypertension.

What Is Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure?

The blood pressure reading is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is written as systolic pressure, the force of the blood against the artery walls as your heart beats, over diastolic pressure, the blood pressure between heartbeats. For example, a blood pressure reading is written as 120/80 mmHg, or “120 over 80”. The systolic pressure is 120 and the diastolic pressure is 80.

NOTE: This blood pressure monitor is suitable for people 12-60 years old, wrist circumference of 13.5-21.5cm.

User Tips
For accurate measurements, please follow below steps to use the blood pressure monitor:
1.Relax for about 5-10 minutes before measuring. Avoid eating, drinking alcohol, smoking, and bathing for 30 minutes before taking measurements (because all this factors will affect the accuracy of the measurements);
2.Roll up your sleeve and make sure your sleeve is not rolled up too tight, remove watch or other ornaments from the measured wrist;
3.Wrap the wrist blood pressure monitor inside your left wrist, make sure the led screen up and towards your face;
4.Please sit in a chair and take an erect body posture, keep the device on the same level with your heart then start measuring. Please don't bend over or cross your legs, or talking until measuring is complete;
5.Read the measured readings and check your blood pressure by referring the WHO classification indicator ;

How to set the users?
Press S button when power off, the screen will display user 1/user 2, press M button to switch from user1 to user2 or user2 to user1, then press S button to confirm the user;

How to set the year, month, date and time?
Continue to above step, it will enter into year setting and the screen will flash 20xx. Press M button to adjust the number from 2001 to 2099, then press S button to confirm and enter into the next setting. The other settings are operated like year setting.

How to read memory records?
Please press the M button when power off, the latest 3 times average value will be shown. Press M again to show the latest memory, press S button to show the oldest memory, as well as subsequent measurements can be shown one after the other by pressing the M button and S button each time.

description:
AQESO wrist blood pressure monitor can be a valuable tool for monitoring your health.

Hypertension doesn't produce any symptoms. You could have dangerously high blood pressure and not even know it.

Thanks to the convenience of the wrist bp monitor, tracking your blood pressure at home is easier and more convenient than ever before.
But wrist bp monitors are extremely sensitive to body position. To get an accurate reading, your arm and wrist must be at heart level while measuring.

How to apply the cuff correctly?

1. Wrap the wrist cuff securely around your wrist. Do not apply the cuff over clothing.

2. Wrap the cuff around whichever wrist is easier to apply to, however, because measurement values vary between the right and left wrists,
make sure to always measure on the same side.

3. Position the cuff leaving a clearance of about 1-1.5cm (1/2 inch) between the cuff and the bottom of your palm.

4. The display needs to be on your inner arm, as your pulse is strongest there. The monitor has a sensor behind the display that takes the reading
by recording your pulse.

5. For the most accurate reading, put your elbow in a relaxed but supported position on table and align your wrist with your heart at same level, then turn the monitor on to take a reading.
Note: You can use the carrying/storage case to support the wrist.

Note:
1. The measurements can be affected by the position of the user, his or her physiologic condition, and other factors, so drinking alcohol or coffee,
eating, smoking, exercising and bathing in 30 minutes should be avoided before you take a measurement.

2. Before measurement, sitting quietly for 15 minutes as measurements taken during a relaxed state will have greater accuracy.

Precautions
1. Before measuring, avoid diet, smoking and various forms of exertion. Before measuring, please sit in a quiet armchair for about 10 minutes and try to find some time to relax. Try to take measurements regularly at the same time of day and always on the same arm；

Attention
The device is not suitable for use on neonatal patients, pregnant women, patients with implanted, electronical devices, patients with pre-eclampsia, premature ventricular beats. Please consult the professionals prior to using the unit if you suffer from illnesses.

Wear correctly

4. Broken heart symbol on screen represents an Arrhythmia condition detected.
5. Automatic power off for power saving.
6. Memory for 3 latest reading.

Instructions For Optimal Readings
1. Maintain a normal heartbeat by resting calm for 5-10 minutes before taking your blood pressure measurement. Avoid consumption of food and alcohol, bath or shower, smoking, exercise, or any physical activities 30 minutes prior to measurement recording.
2. Wrap the cuff on your left arm above the elbow. For accurate measurement, keep the cuff at the same level of your heart.
3. Do not cross your legs. Settle yourself in a sitting position with your back straight and your feet parallel to the floor.
4. Stretch your arm on a flat surface like a table, with your palm facing up.
5. You are now ready to start. For more accurate measurement, avoid any speech while the machine is operating.
6. We recommend a minimum of 15 minutes interval between recordings.

FAQs
Q1: Why are my readings at home different from the hospital?
A: Some objective factors may affect the accuracy: measuring position (crossed legs), emotion, talking, eating, smoking, drinking, exercise,etc.
Q2: How to set the users?
A: Press S button when power off, the screen will display user 1/user 2, press M button to switch from user 1 to user 2 or user 2 to user 1, then press S button to confirm the user.

While the cause of high blood pressure in most people remains unclear, a variety of conditions – such as getting little or no exercise, poor diet, obesity, older age, and genetics – can contribute to the development of hypertension.

What Is Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure?

The blood pressure reading is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is written as systolic pressure, the force of the blood against the artery walls as your heart beats, over diastolic pressure, the blood pressure between heartbeats. For example, a blood pressure reading is written as 120/80 mmHg, or “120 over 80”. The systolic pressure is 120 and the diastolic pressure is 80.

Tips to Monitor Blood Pressure at Home:
The blood pressure in the morning can be significantly different than at night, or when you visit a doctor’s office. Your numbers often change depending on posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions or sleep. To get a more accurate assessment of your blood pressure, we suggest you to measure your blood pressure at the same time every day with peace of mind and follow the tips before you get started.
-Avoid food, caffeine, alcohol, or tobacco products for 30 minutes prior to measuring.
-Rest and sit up straight with your back against the chair, legs uncrossed, feet flat on the floor.
-Place your forearm on an armrest or table with palm of your hand facing up.
-After sitting quietly for five minutes, wrap the cuff snugly around the upper part of your bare left arm. The lower edge of the cuff should be about 1 inch above the bend of your elbow. Use the Velcro wrap to make the cuff snug, but not too tight.
-If you want to repeat the measurement, please wait at least 10 minutes before re-inflating the cuff.

Find the Right Cuff:
Cuff size is also very important in ensuring an accurate reading every time you monitor.
The inflatable part of the sleeve should fit around 80 percent of your upper arm.
To determine your arm size, use a cloth measuring tape and measure the circumference of your left upper arm midway between your elbow and shoulder.

description:
Precautions
1. Before measuring, avoid diet, smoking and various forms of exertion. Before measuring, please sit in a quiet armchair for about 10 minutes and try to find some time to relax. Try to take measurements regularly at the same time of day and always on the same arm；
2. Sit for 5 minutes before the measurement, bare the upper arm of the left or right hand, introduce the left (right) arm into the cuff, the cuff air tube is measured toward the palm of the hand, and the arm is placed flat on the desktop with the palm upward;
3. Sit upright, the body should not be in a state of tension, and should be relaxed. The center of the armband is at the same height as the heart, the armband's gas nozzle should not be twisted down, the surveyor should not speak or twist, move the body.

Attention
The device is not suitable for use on neonatal patients, pregnant women, patients with implanted, electronical devices, patients with pre-eclampsia, premature ventricular beats. Please consult the professionals prior to using the unit if you suffer from illnesses.

Wear correctly
When wearing, the blood pressure band of the arm to be measured should not be too tight. The tracheal outlet should be in the middle of the arm, the edge of the cuff should be 2-3 cm away from the elbow, and the position of the air pipe should be on the extension of the middle finger.

What does mean"E-1,E-2,E-3,E-5"？(Page 11 in the user manual)
E-1: Weak signal and pressure change suddenly.①Wrap the cuff properly;②Remeasure with correct way.
E-2: External strong disturbance. ①When near cell phone or other high radiant device the measurement will be failed;②Keep quiet and no chatting when measuring.
E-3: Cuff leak. ①Wrap the cuff properly;②Make sure the air plug is properly inserted in the unit and then remaeausre.
E-5: Abnormal blood pressure. Repeat the measurement after relax for 30 mins.

Additional Features
1. Automatic measuring design, measures intelligently and provides quick readings within one minute.

4. Broken heart symbol on screen represents an Arrhythmia condition detected.

Instructions For Optimal Readings
1. Maintain a normal heartbeat by resting calm for 5-10 minutes before taking your blood pressure measurement. Avoid consumption of food and alcohol, bath or shower, smoking, exercise, or any physical activities 30 minutes prior to measurement recording.
2. Wrap the cuff on your left arm above the elbow. For accurate measurement, keep the cuff at the same level of your heart.
3. Do not cross your legs. Settle yourself in a sitting position with your back straight and your feet parallel to the floor.
4. Stretch your arm on a flat surface like a table, with your palm facing up.
5. You are now ready to start. For more accurate measurement, avoid any speech while the machine is operating.
6. We recommend a minimum of 15 minutes interval between recordings.

Q1: Why are my readings at home different from the hospital?
A: Some objective factors may affect the accuracy: measuring position (crossed legs), emotion, talking, eating, smoking, drinking, exercise,etc.
Q2: How to set the users?
A: Press S button when power off, the screen will display user 1/user 2, press M button to switch from user 1 to user 2 or user 2 to user 1, then press S button to confirm the user.

How to get accurate reading:    

The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise.Blood pressure wanders all over the map throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, meals, and moods.

We suggest to measure at around the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm 2cm (approximately 2 finger-breadths) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the centre of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull the end of the cuff so that it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ our manual as detail as possible to be instructed regularly!

Masked Hypertention & White-coat Hypertention:

Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn’t always provide accurate  information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and average them.

title: Ruby's Story: An Embryo Adoption Journey by W. Kathryn Clark (2014-05-03)
description:
This heartwarming story describes the journey of how one family comes together through the miracle of Embryo Adoption. 

We join a mother recounting her embryo adoption journey to her daughter, Ruby, who is now around 5 years old. The mother is a single woman who was never able to find her "special someone" to start a family with; she is introduced to the donating family through a friend. The story provides an age-appropriate explanation of IVF, embryo adoption and genetic relationships, and also focuses on the social aspect of adoption.

In the US alone there are half-a-million frozen embryos in storage that have been created for IVF. Once family building is complete, many parents struggle with the decision of what the next steps are  for their frozen embryos. Embryo Adoption is a unique opportunity for couples and individuals experiencing infertility to build their own family by giving these embryos a home.

description:
Blood Pressure is the pressure that flowing blood exerts on the arteries. The heart contracts and relaxes, creating two levels of blood pressure. SYSTOLIC pressure is the highest level of blood pressure, it is the level of pressure when the heart contracts. DIASTOLIC pressure is the lowest level of blood pressure, it is the level of pressure when the heart relaxes. Blood pressure values are measured in millimeters of mercury (written as mmHg). For example, if your blood pressure is 126/76, the systolic pressure is 126 mmHg, and the diastolic pressure is 76 mmHg. High blood pressure, or hypertension, is a level of blood pressure consistently above normal. Most doctors consider a "normal" blood pressure reading for an adult to be 120/80, although it varies according to the individual. Standards for assessment of high or low blood pressure, without regard to age, have been established by the World Health Organization.
When blood pressure is measured in a doctor's office or clinical setting it may cause nervousness or stress in the patient which can produce inaccurate, higher blood pressure rates. This is commonly known as the "white coat" syndrome. Home measurement reduces the effect outside factors might have on blood pressure readings. Self-monitoring is a good way to keep track of your own blood pressure, but it is also very helpful to your doctor. It provides a comprehensive view of the blood pressure changes over a period of time and can help in evaluating the possibility of hypertension.
Though there are many digital blood pressure monitors, there are also many prople who prefer checking blood pressure manually. That's where the Lumiscope 100-021 fits the bill. description:
NOTE: This blood pressure monitor is suitable for people 12-60 years old, wrist circumference of 13.5-21.5cm.

User Tips
For accurate measurements, please follow below steps to use the blood pressure monitor:
1.Relax for about 5-10 minutes before measuring. Avoid eating, drinking alcohol, smoking, and bathing for 30 minutes before taking measurements (because all this factors will affect the accuracy of the measurements);
2.Roll up your sleeve and make sure your sleeve is not rolled up too tight, remove watch or other ornaments from the measured wrist;
3.Wrap the wrist blood pressure monitor inside your left wrist, make sure the led screen up and towards your face;
4.Please sit in a chair and take an erect body posture, keep the device on the same level with your heart then start measuring. Please don't bend over or cross your legs, or talking until measuring is complete;
5.Read the measured readings and check your blood pressure by referring the WHO classification indicator ;

How to set the users?
Press S button when power off, the screen will display user 1/user 2, press M button to switch from user1 to user2 or user2 to user1, then press S button to confirm the user;

How to set the year, month, date and time?
Continue to above step, it will enter into year setting and the screen will flash 20xx. Press M button to adjust the number from 2001 to 2099, then press S button to confirm and enter into the next setting. The other settings are operated like year setting.

How to read memory records?
Please press the M button when power off, the latest 3 times average value will be shown. Press M again to show the latest memory, press S button to show the oldest memory, as well as subsequent measurements can be shown one after the other by pressing the M button and S button each time.

How to get accurate reading:    

The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise. Blood pressure wanders all over the map throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, meals, and moods.

We suggest to measure at around the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm 2cm (approximately 2 finger-breadths) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the centre of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull the end of the cuff so that it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ our manual as detail as possible to be instructed regularly!


Masked Hypertention & White-coat Hypertention:

Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn’t always provide accurate  information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and average them.

What are the benefits of checking blood pressure daily?

Risk of high blood pressure increase with age; however, high blood pressure doesn’t have any signs or symptoms, and it doesn’t discriminate by age.

Routine monitoring can provide your healthcare provider with important information to determine if you have high blood pressure and what treatment plan to recommend.

After-sales Service Guarantee
We have a very supportive service team. We will answer any of your questions and will solve any problems with the device that may occur.


How to use a wrist sphygmomanometer?
➀ Remove objects from your left wrist and wrap the cuff comfortably.
➁ The distance between the cuff and the hand should be about 10mm.
➂ Leave about a half inch between your wrist and cuff.
➃ Lay your arm flat (palm upwards).
➄ Ensure that the cuff is at the same the height as the heart.
➅ Press the ON/OFF button, the measurement begins.

description:
Blood Pressure is the pressure that flowing blood exerts on the arteries. The heart contracts and relaxes, creating two levels of blood pressure. SYSTOLIC pressure is the highest level of blood pressure, it is the level of pressure when the heart contracts. DIASTOLIC pressure is the lowest level of blood pressure, it is the level of pressure when the heart relaxes. Blood pressure values are measured in millimeters of mercury (written as mmHg). For example, if your blood pressure is 126/76, the systolic pressure is 126 mmHg, and the diastolic pressure is 76 mmHg. High blood pressure, or hypertension, is a level of blood pressure consistently above normal. Most doctors consider a "normal" blood pressure reading for an adult to be 120/80, although it varies according to the individual. Standards for assessment of high or low blood pressure, without regard to age, have been established by the World Health Organization.
When blood pressure is measured in a doctor's office or clinical setting it may cause nervousness or stress in the patient which can produce inaccurate, higher blood pressure rates. This is commonly known as the "white coat" syndrome. Home measurement reduces the effect outside factors might have on blood pressure readings. Self-monitoring is a good way to keep track of your own blood pressure, but it is also very helpful to your doctor. It provides a comprehensive view of the blood pressure changes over a period of time and can help in evaluating the possibility of hypertension.
Though there are many digital blood pressure monitors, there are also many prople who prefer checking blood pressure manually. That's where the Lumiscope 100-021 fits the bill. It doesn't require an electric power supply or batteries. It's very affordable. More than that, you can use it anywhere - even on long vacations. description:
INSTANT MONITORING
This FDA Approved with Large Screen Display Clinical Digital Wrist Blood Pressure Monitor Cuffs is designed to make your blood pressure monitoring simple, quick and easy at all times.

Why the blood pressure readings is different every time?
Human blood pressure will change in a very short time due to normal physiological reactions, so the blood pressure may also change during measuring, re-measurement should be in 5 minutes. In fact, even the same doctor continuously measures blood pressure 3-4 times, he will get a different measurement too.

Correct Blood Pressure Measurement Steps
Step 1: Relax in a quiet environment for 5 minutes before measuring blood pressure, if necessary, take a few deep breaths to keep your heart rate steady.

Step 2: Sit quietly in an upright position with legs uncrossed and feet flat on the floor.

Step 3: Keep the position of the cuff at the same height of your heart, meanwhile the cuff's tube off-center towards the inner side of the arm (in line with your pink finger) and close the cuff. The cuff shouldn't be too tight or loose. To test the cuff's fit, snugly insert one index finger between the cuff and your arm.

Step 4: Naturally put your hand on table and let your palm face up. Do not talk or move your body when measuring.

Step 5: Human blood pressure is a changing parameter. Theoretically, there will be little differences between each
measurement. It is the best, however, to re-measure once or twice and choose the average value. Re-measurement should be carried out after 5 to 10 minutes.

description:
INSTANT MONITORING
This FDA Approved with Large Screen Display Clinical Digital Wrist Blood Pressure Monitor Cuffs is designed to make your blood pressure monitoring simple, quick and easy at all times.

Why the blood pressure readings is different every time?
Human blood pressure will change in a very short time due to normal physiological reactions, so the blood pressure may also change during measuring, re-measurement should be in 5 minutes. In fact, even the same doctor continuously measures blood pressure 3-4 times, he will get a different measurement too.

Correct Blood Pressure Measurement Steps
Step 1: Relax in a quiet environment for 5 minutes before measuring blood pressure, if necessary, take a few deep breaths to keep your heart rate steady.

Step 2: Sit quietly in an upright position with legs uncrossed and feet flat on the floor.

Step 3: Keep the position of the cuff at the same height of your heart, meanwhile the cuff's tube off-center towards the inner side of the arm (in line with your pink finger) and close the cuff. The cuff shouldn't be too tight or loose. To test the cuff's fit, snugly insert one index finger between the cuff and your arm.

Step 4: Naturally put your hand on table and let your palm face up. Do not talk or move your body when measuring.

Step 5: Human blood pressure is a changing parameter. Theoretically, there will be little differences between each
measurement. It is the best, however, to re-measure once or twice and choose the average value. Re-measurement should be carried out after 5 to 10 minutes.

MEASUREMENT PROCEDURE

• Position the monitor at the same level as your heart during measurement to ensure accurate readings

• Blood pressure changes with every heartbeat and is in constant fluctuation throughout the day

Steps for an accurate reading:
The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise. Blood pressure can vary throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, your diet, and changes in mood.

We suggest taking measurements close to the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm approximately 1 finger-width (2cm) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the center of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull at the end of the cuff so it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ the user manual in as much detail as possible regularly to ensure proper use.

Masked Hypertension & White-coat Hypertension:
Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn't always provide accurate information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and record their average.

How to get accurate reading:    

The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise. Blood pressure wanders all over the map throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, meals, and moods.

We suggest to measure at around the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm 2cm (approximately 2 finger-breadths) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the centre of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull the end of the cuff so that it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ our manual as detail as possible to be instructed regularly!


Masked Hypertention & White-coat Hypertention:

Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn’t always provide accurate  information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and average them.

Note: A diagnosis of high blood pressure must be confirmed with a medical professional. A doctor should also evaluate any unusually low blood pressure readings

While the cause of high blood pressure in most people remains unclear, a variety of conditions – such as getting little or no exercise, poor diet, obesity, older age, and genetics – can contribute to the development of hypertension.

What Is Systolic and Diastolic Blood Pressure?

The blood pressure reading is measured in millimeters of mercury (mmHg) and is written as systolic pressure, the force of the blood against the artery walls as your heart beats, over diastolic pressure, the blood pressure between heartbeats. For example, a blood pressure reading is written as 120/80 mmHg, or “120 over 80”. The systolic pressure is 120 and the diastolic pressure is 80.

Your SpO2 (peripheral capillary O2) is an estimation of the amount of oxygen in your blood. An SpO2 reading of 95% or greater is generally considered to be a normal oxygen level. However, an SpO2 reading of 92% or less (at sea level) suggests that your blood is poorly saturated. Insufficient saturation can cause a range of adverse health conditions—including chest pain, shortness of breath and increased heart rate., Heart Rate Monitor - The basic way to calculate your maximum heart rate is to subtract your age from 220. For example, if you're 45 years old, subtract 45 from 220 to get a maximum heart rate of 175. This is the maximum number of times your heart should beat per minute during exercise. For adults 18 and older, a normal resting heart rate is between 60 and 100 beats per minute (bpm), depending on the person's physical condition and age., Steps Taken Monitor - How does The Nautilus fitness tracker measure steps? Our Easy-Wrap Cuff comfortably wraps around standard and larger arms, 8.7\" to 15.7\" in circumference.

The blood pressure changes are not always noticeable. However, high or low blood pressure can cause serious diseases,
such as heart attack or stroke. Moreover, the innormal blood pressure can be a symptom of many diseases.
So it is important to record changes in blood pressure every day.
3. Why does my blood pressure fluctuate throughout the day?
Individual blood pressure varies multiple times every day. If the person takes medicine, the pressure will vary more.

Wait at least 3 minutes for another measurement.

Steps for an accurate reading:
The fact that blood pressure measurements vary is no surprise. Blood pressure can vary throughout the day and responds dynamically to movements, your diet, and changes in mood.

We suggest taking measurements close to the same time each day. Place the cuff on your exposed arm approximately 1 finger-width (2cm) above the elbow. Make sure the tubing is placed at the center of your arm facing the front, and that the sensor is correctly placed. Pull at the end of the cuff so it is wrapped evenly and firmly around your arm.

IMPORTANT: Please READ the user manual in as much detail as possible regularly to ensure proper use.

Masked Hypertension & White-coat Hypertension:
Your blood pressure can vary depending on changes in posture, exercise, diet, medications, emotions, or sleep. That’s why a single blood pressure measurement taken at the doctor's office doesn't always provide accurate information about your health. To get a more accurate assessment of blood pressure, people should perform multiple recordings and record their average.

Frequently Asked Questions and Answers:
1. Will the cuff fit large arms?
Our Easy-Wrap Cuff comfortably wraps around standard and larger arms, 8.7\" to 15.7\" in circumference.
Measure your upper arm with a cloth tape measure to determine the best fit.
2. Why is it important to monitor blood pressure everyday?
The blood pressure changes are not always noticeable. However, high or low blood pressure can cause serious diseases,
such as heart attack or stroke. Moreover, the innormal blood pressure can be a symptom of many diseases.
So it is important to record changes in blood pressure every day.
3. Why does my blood pressure fluctuate throughout the day?
Individual blood pressure varies multiple times every day. If the person takes medicine, the pressure will vary more.
It is also affected by the way you apply the cuff and measurement position, so please take the measurement under the same condition.
Wait at least 3 minutes for another measurement.
